stem.text: The power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\left(x - 5\right)^{n}}{4^{n} \left(n^{\frac{1}{3}} + 4\right)} \) has radius of convergence \( 4 \). Determine whether the series converges or diverges at \( x = 1 \), naming the test used.

answer_key.label: At \( x = 1 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{1}{3}} + 4} \) decrease to 0.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 5\right| < 4 \), so the left endpoint is \( x = 1 \).
At \( x = 1 \), \( \frac{\left(x - 5\right)^{n}}{4^{n}} = \left(\frac{-4}{4}\right)^{n} = (-1)^{n} \), so the series becomes \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{n^{\frac{1}{3}} + 4} \).
The terms alternate in sign, their sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{1}{3}} + 4} \) decrease as n increases, and \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n^{\frac{1}{3}} + 4} = 0 \).
At \( x = 1 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{1}{3}} + 4} \) decrease to 0, so \( x = 1 \) belongs to the interval of convergence.

options.label: At \( x = 1 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{1}{3} \le 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series test used on the alternating endpoint series, whose terms are not all positive

options.label: At \( x = 1 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{\frac{1}{3}} + 4} \) has \( p = \frac{1}{3} \le 1 \).
options.derivation: the factor (-1)^n produced by substituting the negative displacement -4 dropped, so the endpoint series was tested with the wrong sign pattern
